name: Subarachnoid space and basal cisterns
summary: The CSF-filled space between the arachnoid and the pia covers the whole brain and spinal cord and widens into cisterns wherever the arachnoid bridges a hollow: the cisterna magna behind the medulla, the pontine and interpeduncular cisterns in front of the brainstem, the suprasellar (chiasmatic) cistern around the optic chiasm and circle of Willis, the ambient and quadrigeminal cisterns around the midbrain, and the Sylvian cisterns. Cranial nerves and the major arteries run through these cisterns, blood collects in them after aneurysm rupture, and their effacement is the imaging sign of herniation.

anatomy.location: Between arachnoid and pia over the entire CNS; the basal cisterns lie between the base of the brain and the skull base from the cisterna magna to the interhemispheric fissure; the space ends at S2 in the spinal canal, where lumbar puncture is performed below the conus.

subdivisions.name: Cisterna magna (cerebellomedullary)
subdivisions.note: between the cerebellum and medulla, receiving CSF from the foramen of Magendie

subdivisions.name: Pontine and interpeduncular cisterns
subdivisions.note: basilar artery, CN VI, III, and the basilar tip

subdivisions.name: Suprasellar (chiasmatic) cistern
subdivisions.note: optic chiasm, infundibulum, circle of Willis

subdivisions.name: Ambient and quadrigeminal cisterns
subdivisions.note: around the midbrain: PCA, SCA, CN IV, vein of Galen

function: Cushions the brain, carries CSF from the fourth ventricle to the arachnoid granulations, and provides the route for the cranial nerves and arteries at the base of the brain.

bestView.label: suprasellar cistern with the circle of Willis
prepontine and ambient cisterns around the brainstem

imaging.normalAppearance: CSF spaces: dark on T1, bright on T2, dark on FLAIR. The basal cisterns should be open and symmetric; effacement of the suprasellar or ambient cisterns signals uncal or central herniation. Blood in the cisterns is bright on non-contrast CT and bright on FLAIR.

pathology.finding: Hyperdense blood in the basal cisterns and Sylvian fissures; the distribution suggests the aneurysm site; FLAIR shows sulcal hyperintensity when CT is negative later.
pathology.timing: CT sensitivity is near 100% in the first 6 h and falls over days

pathology.finding: Loss of the suprasellar and perimesencephalic cisterns with a mass or diffuse swelling.
Thick enhancement of the basal cisterns with cranial nerve palsies and hydrocephalus.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Non-contrast CT for blood and herniation; FLAIR and T1+Gd for meningeal disease

lesionEffects.mechanism: Basal meningitis or cisternal tumor spread coating the nerves
Herniation compressing the cisterns and the brainstem

examination: Neck stiffness, Kernig and Brudzinski signs
Fundoscopy for subhyaloid hemorrhage and papilledema
pearls: Blood in the interhemispheric fissure suggests an AComm aneurysm; in the Sylvian fissure an MCA aneurysm; in front of the pons a basilar or vertebral source
Lumbar puncture samples the same space: xanthochromia confirms subarachnoid hemorrhage when CT is negative after 12 hours
